problem: Existing image-goal (target-driven) navigation methods (DRL/IL) assume static environments, so moving obstacles such as other robots corrupt spatial reasoning and cause collisions. Dynamic-obstacle avoidance methods are only local planners that get trapped and cannot search for an image-specified target.
motivation: Search-and-rescue style scenarios need robots to find people or objects given only a target image in unknown, cluttered, dynamic scenes, while avoiding other robots. No end-to-end learning method handled target-driven navigation in dynamic unknown environments, so the task is decomposed into exploration and collision avoidance, where good demonstrations are available.
key_idea: An end-to-end Decision-Transformer-based navigation policy with dual BYOL-trained visual encoders (a static encoder for layout, a general encoder for obstacles), cross-task trained on exploration and multi-robot collision avoidance demonstrations.
insight: Ablations show every design choice matters: removing the general encoder or the SSL-trained encoders drops SR (48.89 to 41.25 and 39.58), removing target hidden-state concatenation drops it to 32.08, and removing exploration trajectories collapses it to 12.08, so exploration is the dominant skill. A pretrained ImageNet ResNet18 replacing the DVE collapses SR to 7.92, showing a domain gap for frozen or pretrained features. Compared to a single-encoder DT, the dual encoders and cross-task training give large gains (12.5 m, 4 robots: SR 26.25 to 48.89).
method: Multi-modal input sequence: target image g plus trajectory of (return-to-go, observation, action) tuples, embedded at d=128 for a GPT-2-style causal transformer
Dual-visual encoders: two 3-layer CNNs on 84x84 RGB; the static encoder f_s extracts layout features, the general encoder f_g extracts obstacle features and encodes the target image

BYOL self-supervised training: the static encoder uses image pairs of the same view with and without dynamic obstacles so it learns only shared static features; the general encoder uses standard augmentation views

Navigation network: 3 causal transformer blocks, 2 heads, context 1024, learnable timestep/modality positional embeddings; a linear layer on the concatenation [h_g; h_obs] (target hidden state concatenation) predicts the velocity action

Cross-task offline training: alternate sampling between exploration data D_e (frontier exploration + A* + DWA, 3,496 trajectories) and collision avoidance data D_ca (NH-ORCA, 7,467 trajectories); MSE action loss plus BYOL loss on D_ssl (98k image pairs)

setting.backbone: Causal transformer (GPT-2 style, 3 blocks) with two small CNN encoders trained from scratch (BYOL)
setting.training_data: Simulated Gazebo data: 3,496 exploration trajectories (342,954 steps), 7,467 collision avoidance trajectories (469,378 steps), 98,000 SSL image pairs; real-world finetune with 50 exploration trajectories, 100 collision avoidance trajectories and 500 image pairs
setting.observation: monocular RGB 84x84 from the onboard camera plus target RGB image
setting.simulator: Gazebo (3D mazes and photorealistic scenes) with Jackal robots
setting.privileged: none at test time (privileged info such as maps and other robots' states is used only for data collection and the FCA upper-bound baseline)

numbers.eval_set_note: 7.5x7.5 m mazes, 2 robots; 60 trials per setup, unseen mazes

numbers.evidence: Table I, 12.5x12.5, 4 robots; also Table IV

numbers.eval_set_note: 3 unseen photorealistic environments (bookstore, cafe, house), 3 Jackal robots, 30 trials each
12.5x12.5 m mazes, TurtleBot3 dynamic obstacles unseen in training
15 trials in a 9x10 m office with 2 Jackal robots
numbers.evidence: NavFormer achieved an SR of 63.33%, SPL of 0.406, and CR of 0.229

numbers_note: Custom benchmarks only (Gazebo). CR is collision rate, lower is better. The FCA baseline uses privileged information and beats NavFormer.
results: NavFormer beats all learned baselines (VRW, DSAC, MA-TDN, DT) in unseen mazes, photorealistic scenes and with unseen dynamic obstacles, e.g. 12.5 m/4 robots SR 48.89% vs DT 26.25%. It stays below the FCA upper bound (frontier + NH-ORCA with maps and robot states), e.g. 73.33% SR in the same setting. Real-world SR is 63.33%.
limitations: Trained and evaluated on simple synthetic targets (colored spheres and boxes); the authors list object recognition backbones for common objects as future work
Dynamic obstacles are only other robots; performance drops in larger environments and out-of-distribution scenes, and remains well below the privileged FCA
Real-world validation is small (15 trials, 2 robots) and needs finetuning on real data
